clue.text: Like Shylock, left abandoned in a sorry state

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter for left is dropped from the word meaning like Shylock

parts.note: Shylock, the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, is miserly

explanation.surface: Shylock, deserted by everyone, is in a pitiful condition at the end of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes L out of MISERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is a wretched condition, a sorry state of unhappiness.

clue.text: Flag mates had unfurled

indicators.note: unfurled, like a flag shaken out, signals that the letters are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: A friend's flag was opened out to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfurled' rearranges MATESHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the top of a mast, where a flag flies; by extension it can mean the flag flown there.

clue.text: Odds on tip failing to start Redcar's opener: that should cool things down

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the odds offered on a horse at the off

indicators.note: failing to start says the first letter of the word for tip is lost

parts.note: a wrinkle is a useful tip or hint

indicators.note: opener points to the first letter of the town name

explanation.surface: A racing tipster's hot favourite at Redcar races fails to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' cuts W from WRINKLE to give RINKLE; 'opener' takes R from Redcar. Redcar is a racecourse town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinkler sprays water on lawns or on a fire, cooling and dampening the area.

clue.text: Possibly acid sweet

definitions.meaning: acid ... is one kind of ... music, so acid is possibly this genre
a hard stick of seaside candy sold at British resorts

explanation.surface: Is this sour thing maybe a sweet, or perhaps an acid drop?
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rock is a psychedelic music style, and a stick of seaside candy is a sweet with a name through it.

clue.text: Laurel; ultimate feed character Hardy flayed as a rule

parts.note: Stan Laurel, the comedian partnered with Oliver Hardy

indicators.note: ultimate picks out the final letter of the word feed
flayed means skinned, so the outer letters of Hardy are removed

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy as a comic double act, with the straight man feeding lines to his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' gives D from feed; 'flayed' strips Hardy to ARD. 'character' and 'as a' are link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a norm or principle laid down, the same as a rule.

clue.text: Burning unopened ancient Chinese book after revolutionary nonsense

indicators.note: after places the book's letters following the turned word
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for nonsense is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: unopened tells us to remove the first letter of the book's title

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese Book of Changes

explanation.surface: A revolutionary burns an ancient Chinese classic without even opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ROT into TOR; 'unopened' drops the I from I CHING to give CHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Torching something is setting it on fire, so torching is burning.

clue.text: Disputed territory, Middle Eastern state separating Northern from Southern region

indicators.note: separating means the state stands between the two compass letters

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
land is a region or country

explanation.surface: A Gulf nation divides north from south in a contested area.
explanation.definitionFit: No man's land is ground between opposing forces that neither side holds, a disputed territory.

clue.text: Distribute every set of books

parts.note: all means every one
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A librarian hands out every volume in a series.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or apportion, the same as distribute.

clue.text: Upwardly mobile Miliband adopts dreadful guy

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving upwards means the letters are read from bottom to top
adopts means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ed Miliband, the former UK Labour leader
dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: An ambitious politician takes on an awful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' puts DIRE inside ED to give EDIRED; 'Upwardly mobile' turns it all upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to mock or ridicule them, which is to deride them.

clue.text: Heathland shrub decaudated French sheepdog

indicators.note: decaudated means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the briard is a French breed of sheepdog

explanation.surface: A French herding dog has had its tail docked out on the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decaudated' removes D from BRIARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Briar is the name for prickly heath plants such as tree heath and wild rose.

clue.text: Smart fraudster, ultimately a deceitful character

parts.note: spruce means neat and smart in appearance

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fraudster

explanation.surface: A well-dressed con man is at heart a dishonest type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart fraudster' reads as the definition, but 'fraudster, ultimately' only supplies R; the definition is the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprucer is old slang for a liar or swindler, someone who tells tall tales: a deceitful character.

clue.text: Perhaps reading thriller writer who goes on a bit?

parts.note: reading is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it
Eric Ambler wrote spy thrillers such as The Mask of Dimitrios

explanation.surface: Is a thriller author long-winded when you read him?
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R is 'reading', marked by 'Perhaps' as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler talks at length without getting to the point, someone who goes on and on.

clue.text: Electronic greeting cards

annotationWithheld.why: Electronic greeting cards (4) for HAND: 'cards' gives a hand and 'greeting' may be a hand, but no reading accounts for 'Electronic'; likely an OCR misread or missing letters, and no source found

clue.text: Friend maintaining another had contrived a plot

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the first friend surrounds the second

parts.note: mate is a friend
china, from rhyming slang china plate for mate, is another word for friend
the contraction 'd stands for had

explanation.surface: A pal shielding another had schemed together.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or plot, so machinated means plotted craftily.

clue.text: Writer producing hesitant utterance by reluctant king, one having abdicated for love, gaining Colin's first Oscar

parts.note: um is the sound made while hesitating

indicators.note: having abdicated for means one letter steps down and another takes its place

parts.note: Bertie was George VI, the reluctant king who took the throne after his brother abdicated
I is the Roman numeral one
O is love, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name Colin

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A biography of a stammering king who unwillingly took the throne, perhaps starring Colin Firth in an Oscar-winning role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abdicated for' swaps the I (one) in BERTIE for O (love), giving BERTOE. The surface recalls The King's Speech, for which Colin Firth won an Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist, author of The Name of the Rose, so a writer.

clue.text: A fabric keeping fellow passionately aroused

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: lame is a fabric woven with metallic threads

explanation.surface: A shimmering cloth keeps a man warm and excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame describes someone burning with intense feeling, ablaze with passion.

clue.text: Language of North American spin

definitions.meaning: the tongue spoken in Britain, the USA and elsewhere
in American pool and billiards, side spin put on the cue ball

explanation.surface: Where did that Canadian tongue get its twist?
explanation.definitionFit: It is the language of England, and in North American billiards the word also names side spin on a ball.

clue.text: Scrap poor misshapen branch

indicators.note: misshapen means twisted out of form, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Throw out that poor deformed tree limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misshapen' rearranges SCRAPPOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporocarp is a spore-bearing body in fungi and ferns, a fruiting branch or outgrowth.

clue.text: Host of insects noticed finally creeping up

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

indicators.note: in a down entry, the final letter creeps up to the top of its word

parts.note: seen means noticed

explanation.surface: A swarm of insects was spotted at last crawling upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally creeping up' moves the last letter of SEEN to its top, giving NSEE, placed below LICE in this down entry. A licensee runs a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee is the licence holder who runs a pub and acts as host to customers.

clue.text: Hosts my City side

definitions.meaning: the team playing on its own ground, entertaining the visitors
the club of my own town or city, the one I support locally

explanation.surface: My local football club is playing at home this weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: The club playing on its own ground hosts the match, and a fan's local club is their own.

clue.text: Drink knocked back in France that's gratis

indicators.note: in places the turned drink inside the other letters

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
i.e., id est, means that is

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the word for drink is reversed

parts.note: beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink downed in France at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns BEER into REEB, which goes in F and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebie is something given free of charge, so it is gratis.

clue.text: Completely enthusiastic about Christian society leaving Church

parts.note: if you are into something you are keen on it

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letters for church are removed

parts.note: Toc H is a Christian charitable movement founded in WWI

explanation.surface: A keen member quits the church but remains wholly committed to the Christian group.
explanation.walkthrough: Toc H is a Christian service society founded in Belgium in 1915; 'leaving' takes CH out of TOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for in total, meaning wholly or entirely.

clue.text: Mother's need for table linen

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal; the 's is read as has
to ask is to require or need, as in 'it asks great patience'

explanation.surface: Mother needs a new tablecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric used for tablecloths and napkins.

clue.text: Hush money reported

indicators.note: reported signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: a piece is a coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Hush money was paid, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hush money' is one phrase in the surface but splits into the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush means calm or quiet, the same as peace.

clue.text: Possibly set in haste, ain't these ultimately contrasts?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A writer asks whether hurried opposites are really just opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges SETINHASTE; 'ain't these ultimately' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Antitheses are direct opposites, things set in contrast.

clue.text: Dynasty originally secured in revolutionary overwhelming defeat

definitions.text: Dynasty originally secured in revolutionary overwhelming defeat

indicators.note: secured in says the letter is held inside the defeat
revolutionary means turning, so the whole result is read upwards

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word Dynasty

explanation.surface: A royal line was established after a crushing victory over the old king.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside ROUT and the whole is turned upward in this down entry. The Tudor line began after Henry VII's victory at Bosworth in 1485.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor royal house was founded when Henry VII defeated Richard III at Bosworth.

clue.text: Prado getting to display Venetian magistrate

indicators.note: to display means the letters are shown within the words around them

explanation.surface: The Madrid gallery acquires a portrait of a Venetian official.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prado is the national art museum in Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the chief magistrate and ruler of the old Venetian republic.

clue.text: River's turbulent bore

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the river to the wordplay

indicators.note: turbulent means churned up, so the letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: A tidal surge crashes up the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is a tidal wave running up an estuary, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river in north-east Spain.

clue.text: Julie, for instance, has written on Prince

indicators.note: written on means set down following the prince's name

parts.note: Andrew is a British prince
the contraction 's stands for has

explanation.surface: An actress has written about a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Julie Andrews is the star of Mary Poppins, so she is an example of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Julie Andrews, the actress, bears this surname, so Julie is one example of it.

clue.text: Steal a vegetable

definitions.meaning: tailors' slang for pocketing offcuts of cloth, so to pilfer
a leafy green such as a savoy

explanation.surface: Pinch a greengrocer's leafy produce.
explanation.definitionFit: In old tailoring slang to cabbage is to pilfer leftover cloth, and it is also a green leafy vegetable.

clue.text: Drunken rake and soak in amateur singsongs

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken libertine and a boozer belt out tunes in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges RAKESOAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is singing along to recorded backing tracks, a pastime for amateur singers.

clue.text: Cannon and Ball

definitions.meaning: a fluffy woollen ball worn on a hat

explanation.surface: The comedy double act Cannon and Ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Cannon and Ball were a British TV comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: The rapid-firing naval gun is named after its sound, and a woolly ball trimming a hat has the same name.
